entries.title: Mangione admits killing healthcare CEO and pleads guilty to federal charges
entries.snippet: "I shot Mr Thompson in Manhattan and he died," the 28-year-old said after pleading guilty to charges of stalking resulting in death.

entries.title: Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule
entries.snippet: Women across the country speak of public floggings, losing their jobs, and barriers to healthcare that endanger lives.

entries.title: US aircraft carrier on way to relieve USS Lincoln after issues reported on board
entries.snippet: Thousands of sailors on the Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.

entries.title: Instagram accounts fuelling Ceuta crisis with paid advice for help to cross
entries.snippet: BBC's Top Comment podcast has found a network of Instagram profiles glamourising the swim around the Morocco-Ceuta border fence.

entries.title: Activists try to deliver aid to Palestinians in homes besieged by Israeli settlers
entries.snippet: Two families have been trapped in their homes in the occupied West Bank for several days.

entries.title: 'Unprecedented' rain in Japan kills eight people
entries.snippet: The storm cut power to more than 20,000 households and left 7,000 people stranded at Tokyo's Narita airport.

entries.title: Builders unearth €9m gold stash sealed in walls of Belgian property
entries.snippet: Construction workers found the stash in the walls of a cellar while drilling to lay sewage pipes.

entries.title: Dozens injured and thousands evacuated in Croatia wildfire
entries.snippet: Officials say the blaze, near the port town of Omis, is one of the worst in Croatia's history.

entries.title: France's top court blocks social media ban for under-15s
entries.snippet: The Constitutional Council says it infringes upon freedom of expression - but President Macron vows to prepare a new draft.

entries.title: Stolen Matisse artworks recovered by police in Brazil
entries.snippet: A man is arrested after eight works by the French artist are found at a home in greater São Paulo.

entries.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to allow ballroom work to continue
entries.snippet: Forcing the US president to go "hat-in-hand to Congress" for permission would be "dangerous", the administration says.

entries.title: Zambia vote counting resumes after pause over alleged attacks on polling staff
entries.snippet: The electoral commission said violence had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers".

entries.title: UK diplomats no longer get hardship bonus for being posted to Buenos Aires
entries.snippet: Civil servants are entitled to extra money for working in difficult or dangerous cities around the world.

entries.title: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms
entries.snippet: Thousands of sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.

entries.title: US says dozens of countries helped China dodge Trump's tariffs
entries.snippet: A new US report said China had moved goods through nations with lower tariffs to dodge higher levies.

entries.title: Engine parts smashed Ryanair window that man's head was sucked out of, report says
entries.snippet: A preliminary report by US investigators says an engine fan blade broke on last month's flight from Greece to Germany.

entries.title: US missionary released following kidnap in Niger, Christian group says
entries.snippet: Kevin Rideout, who was kidnapped outside his home in the capital last October, is now with US officials.

entries.title: Palestinians told to leave homes in village where Israeli settlers besieged houses
entries.snippet: The mayor of Qusra says Israeli troops have been telling families to leave their houses, using some as barracks.

entries.title: Person fined after using foghorn to wake sleeping polar bear
entries.snippet: Under local regulations in the region, "it is forbidden to needlessly disturb, attract or pursue a polar bear".

entries.title: Romania shuts only nuclear plant as heat causes huge drop in Danube River level
entries.snippet: The Cernavodă plant, which produces 20% of Romania's electricity, is not expected to be restarted within the next 10 days.

entries.title: How Americans deceive ourselves about slavery
entries.snippet: Clint Smith's How the Word Is Passed explores how slavery is — and isn't — taught. And Above Ground includes poems to his children about what their ancestors endured and escaped. He spoke with Fresh Air in 2021 and 2023.

entries.title: As speed cameras spread to more states, so does the backlash from drivers
entries.snippet: Millions of drivers across the country are encountering speed cameras for the first time, or will soon. Some don't like it, but advocates say there's clear evidence that cameras make roads safer.

entries.title: Is there a summer COVID-19 surge this year? Yep, it's ramping up again
entries.snippet: Just like all previous summers since the pandemic began, COVID-19 cases are ticking up again, even while other health threats make more headlines.

entries.title: Mangione pleads guilty in federal court, leaving fate of state trial uncertain
entries.snippet: Mangione has pleaded guilty to stalking charges in connection with the death of Brian Thompson, a health care executive. A separate judge will decide the future of Mangione's state trial.

entries.title: We learned 5 important things about the economy this week
entries.snippet: From inflation, to credit card debt, to who's actually doing the spending: These are key takeaways from this week in economic news.

entries.title: The Taliban has taken a terrible toll on the education of girls -- and boys as well
entries.snippet: Saturday marks the 5th anniversary of the current Taliban rule in Aghanistan. They've had a devastating impact on girls' education. A lesser told story is their impact on the education of boys.

entries.title: U.S. missionary who was kidnapped in Niger is released
entries.snippet: Kevin Rideout "is in good health in the care of US officials," SIM International said in a statement, adding he would soon be reunited with his family.

entries.title: Feds probe 'mention markets.' And, lawmakers call for investigation into USS Lincoln
entries.snippet: Federal regulators are reviewing 'mention markets' that allow wagers on what public figures will say. And, Democratic lawmakers call for an investigation into conditions on the long-deployed USS Lincoln.

entries.title: Sen. Ruben Gallego on handling of USS Lincoln conditions: 'That's not proper leadership'
entries.snippet: Lawmakers want answers from the Pentagon chief and the U.S. Navy about living conditions aboard the USS Lincoln. NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona.

entries.title: From Europe to Asia, floods to heatwaves, world experiences weather shocks
entries.snippet: At least eight people died in Japan as heavy rains flooded roads and disrupted traffic while firefighters from Britain to France and Croatia struggled to contain blazes in Europe's fifth heatwave this summer

entries.title: Army temporarily halts Apache helicopter training missions after deadly Texas crash
entries.snippet: No cause of the Wednesday crash has been released because the investigation has just begun. A safety investigation team from the Army Combat Readiness Center in Fort Rucker, Alabama, is trying to determine what happened, the Army said.

entries.title: Jason Arday, youngest Black professor at Cambridge, found dead at 41 after resignation
entries.snippet: A British sociologist who resigned last week from the University of Cambridge following weeks of public accusations of plagiarism and media scrutiny was found dead Friday.

entries.title: New aircraft carrier en route to Middle East after issues reported aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
entries.snippet: The Lincoln has been supporting the U.S. war against Iran, and its deployment has included a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea of more than 240 days.

entries.title: Luigi Mangione reveals motive for CEO's killing after pleading guilty in federal case
entries.snippet: In a surprise turn, Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to the shooting death of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. Mangione admitted he stalked and shot Thompson in 2024 outside a Hilton hotel in Manhattan. He potentially faces life in prison. The 28-year-old is also still facing st

entries.title: Trump dismisses concerns over conditions on long-deployed USS Abraham Lincoln
entries.snippet: Reports from sailors and their families describe concerning conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. The ship has been at sea since last November, a record-length deployment. White House correspondent Liz Landers reports.

entries.title: Quick-thinking controller helps 2 planes with same flight number avoid possible disaster
entries.snippet: A potential disaster was averted Friday when a Phoenix air traffic controller recognized two American Airlines jets mistakenly were flying the same flight number and acted quickly to avoid confusion and keep them a safe distance apart.

entries.title: News Wrap: Record-breaking heat wave grips Europe

entries.title: Congo Ebola outbreak on track to become deadliest in history
entries.snippet: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to worsen, with the number of confirmed cases climbing to over 4,600. At least 2,100 people have died, a death toll that was reached almost three times faster than the outbreak over a decade ago. William Brangham di

entries.title: Greece toughens stance on illegal migration with new deportation plan
entries.snippet: Eleven years into a migration crisis, Greece is trying to stop boats crossing from North Africa to the Greek island of Crete. Five European Union countries have made a breakthrough in their efforts to deport migrants crossing the Mediterranean Sea. Uganda in East Africa has agree

entries.title: Brooks and Atkins Stohr on 'woke' politics in America
entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Kimberly Atkins Stohr of the Boston Globe join William Brangham to discuss the week in politics, including the surprising result in Wisconsin's Democratic primary, the status of 'woke' politics in America and the stalemate between the U.S. and Ira

entries.title: Palestinians besieged in West Bank village of Qusra fear Israeli settlers will seize their homes
entries.snippet: The standoff in Qusra between Palestinian families and Israeli settlers who apparently want to push them out entered a new stage Friday as activists supporting the Palestinians marched toward the besieged homes to replenish their dwindling food and water supply.

entries.title: Ancient Nero's Bridge reemerges from Tiber River as Rome faces water crisis
entries.snippet: Named for the former Roman emperor, the bridge once connected Rome's city center with the Tiber's right bank.

entries.title: NTSB says broken engine parts shattered Ryanair plane window that a man's head got sucked into
entries.snippet: A fan blade in the Boeing 737-800's right engine broke loose, sending fragments flying out of the engine that broke the window and damaged the fuselage in several other places, according to a preliminary report by the National Transportation Safety Board.

entries.title: Trump's vaccine order would require millions of individual shots last used decades ago
entries.snippet: Monday's announcement by Trump calls for separating combination shots — including the measles, mumps and rubella, or MMR, vaccine — into separate injections.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump says USS Lincoln's deployment was 'not nearly long enough'
entries.snippet: Trump refuted that family members have raised concerns about the deployment's length and even said that the more than 260-day deployment is "not nearly long enough."

entries.title: France's top court blocks under-15 social media ban, citing constitutional freedoms
entries.snippet: France last month became the first country in the European Union to pass a blanket ban on the platforms amid rising worldwide concerns about the harmful effects of digital content on kids.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump highlights violent crime reduction during visit to NY police academy
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump highlighted his record on crime and safety during a visit to New York on Friday, pivoting to one of his strongest issues as he looks to boost Republicans in battleground races ahead of the November midterms.

entries.title: Russian drones kill a woman and 9-year-old son at home as Ukrainian civilian casualties surge
entries.snippet: This attack comes after the United Nations reported that July was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since the early weeks of Russia's invasion.

entries.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal stalking charges in the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO
entries.snippet: "On the morning of Dec. 4, 2024, I shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan, and he died," Mangione told the Manhattan federal court, which he entered shackled at the feet but not handcuffed in his beige jail uniform.

entries.title: U.S. retail sales unexpectedly post largest drop in more than a year
entries.snippet: The drop in spending raised concern among some economists about the resiliency of consumers who have powered the economy forward despite nagging inflation and soaring gasoline prices.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Donald Trump to declare Hormuz US territory 'soon'
entries.snippet: Donald Trump said the strait would become part of the US after Iran is defeated. He also told Americans to accept higher gas prices, which have soared since Iran closed Hormuz in response to US and Israeli attacks.

entries.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to let White House ballroom construction continue
entries.snippet: Justice Department lawyers echoed the US president's claim that the $400 million White House ballroom ​project is a security necessity.

entries.title: Jason Arday: Ex-Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism scandal found dead
entries.snippet: Jason Arday, the youngest ever Black professor at Cambridge, was found unresponsive at an address in London. Arday had recently resigned in the midst of a plagiarism row.

entries.title: Vast German wildfire forces evacuation in Eifel forest
entries.snippet: Firefighters tackling the biggest forest fire in the history of North-Rhine Westfalia say residents are unlikely to be able to return on Friday amid high temperatures, humidity and wind. DW has the latest.

entries.title: In Germany record heat meets climate action fatigue
entries.snippet: For the German government climate action does not seem to be a priority — despite record temperatures, heat-related deaths and drought. Why don't more people take to the streets in protest?

entries.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal stalking charges in Brian Thompson death
entries.snippet: The plea resolves the remaining federal charges tied to the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson and could affect a separate New York state case.

entries.title: Germany news: Car industry hemorrhaging jobs
entries.snippet: The country's famed auto sector is losing jobs faster than any industrial branch in the economy, official statistics show. Meanwhile, farmers say drought conditions could affect this year's harvest. DW has more.

entries.title: France: Top watchdog blocks social media ban for children
entries.snippet: Denying access to platforms such as Facebook, TikTok and YouTube for under-15s would infringe upon freedom of expression, the Constitutional Council has said.

entries.title: Eco wins: A Dutch lab for crops, a climate-ready city, and a beaver comeback
entries.snippet: Dutch crops hit the "climate gym," a German city is preparing for more extreme weather, and beavers are restoring rivers across Europe. This week's eco wins are all about building and adapting to a changing climate.

entries.title: Taliban pressured by insurgents after 5 years in power
entries.snippet: The Taliban managed to retake power in Afghanistan on August 15, 2021. Now, they face armed factions who challenge the Taliban rule and strain their central claim of providing security.

entries.title: Congo: Ebola cases are rising at record pace
entries.snippet: The Ebola virus is spreading rapidly in the DRC. In Kinshasa, a city of millions, fears of a serious health crisis are growing. Hospitals are scrambling to prepare for emergencies as best as they can.

entries.title: Fact check: False claims target US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
entries.snippet: Abdul El-Sayed, who could become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate if he wins in November, has been targeted by false claims online following his victory in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary.

entries.title: Can a giant Madonna help slow secularization in Poland?
entries.snippet: Europe's largest statue of the Virgin Mary will be inaugurated on Saturday in the Polish village of Konotopie. What will the monument mean for the village it towers over and for the Catholic faith in Poland in general?

entries.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Latvia
entries.snippet: Jets have shot down a foreign drone over Latvia after it entered the Baltic state's airspace. Its origin remains unclear, but the incident adds to concern over repeated incursions along NATO's eastern flank.

entries.title: Zambia vote count resumes after suspension amid reports of violence
entries.snippet: Earlier, the electoral commission suspended vote counting after alleged attacks on polling staff and the theft of marked ballot papers.

entries.title: Berlin's Russian House: A hub for propaganda and espionage?
entries.snippet: The Russian House stands in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it's being used to spread propaganda for Putin's Russia. Now, French authorities have said it is being used by the Kremlin for espionage.

entries.title: Why women are breaking men's endurance records
entries.snippet: Sophie Woods has completed the 2,000-kilometer Via Alpina faster even than the fastest-ever man. DW explains why she is not the only woman breaking men's records in extreme sports.

entries.title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'
entries.snippet: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.

entries.title: UK: Nigel Farage beats a trash can in Clacton by-election
entries.snippet: Nigel Farage reclaimed his Clacton seat with 63% of the vote, but his main rival, Count Binface, took over a quarter, as Farage skipped the count citing security concerns.
